activeFindings.title: Validate and bind the receiving Input as a canonical receiver-owned record
activeFindings.finding: qualifyExternalWork reads receiverSource with the generic readSource API and checks only kind, inputKind, projectId and workId on receiver.document. It does not validate the common Input schema, domainId, record id/origin or membership in the selected receiving Work. The later validateGitWorkRecords call validates listed Work records; it does not turn arbitrary source documents outside that record set into canonical Inputs. A completed local gate with a Verification hash for such a document is sufficient for the helper to return qualified:true.
activeFindings.reproduction: The real unchanged final helper was called with memory-only source readers and the real canonical record validator. Both producer and consumer Work validations passed. A receiver document outside the Work record set, carrying the wrong domain and then additionally omitting schema, id and origin, was still accepted. The same fixture with a valid canonical receiving Input is accepted as the positive control. This is not claimed as a Git-backed or native-authentication exploit.
activeFindings.impact: A source file that has never passed the required canonical Input identity/attribution checks can satisfy the receiving qualification boundary. This weakens the stated receiver-owned evidence contract even though native authentication, shared delivery and execution authority remain explicitly false.

activeFindings.introducedBy: New futureBehaviorChecks perfect-score case in verification-plan-r2.json
activeFindings.title: Separate verified perfect-score clinic eligibility from teacher-review completion in the new test oracle
activeFindings.finding: The new case says a 100-point observation without verified exact assessment identity OR teacher review should produce no automatic clinic exemption, print or final completion. As written, the missing-teacher-review branch also denies the default clinic exclusion for an otherwise verified, correctly scoped 100-point assessment. The preserved perfect-score rule says that assessment is excluded from default wrong/similar clinic targets, while teacher review, correction, printing and distribution remain independent. A scoped teacher exception is separate.
activeFindings.impact: The acceptance oracle combines two different decisions. An implementation following its literal OR condition can keep a verified perfect-score assessment in the default clinic queue merely because teacher review is unknown, even though the actual rule only prohibits inferring review/print/completion from the score. This is a planning/test-contract conflict; no production behavior was executed or claimed.
activeFindings.repair: Split the oracle into distinct cases: unverified assessment identity plus a 100-point value cannot establish exemption; a verified exact-scope 100-point assessment is excluded from default clinic targets while teacher review remains unknown and printing/distribution/completion are not inferred; an explicit scoped teacher exception is represented separately. If the intended case required both identity and review to be missing, remove the ambiguous OR wording and still add the valid-score/unknown-review positive case.
repairAcceptance: Verified exact assessment score 100 plus unknown teacher review produces default clinic exclusion without declaring teacher review or physical effects complete.
A score with unresolved assessment identity does not establish exemption.
A separately scoped teacher exception affects only its named target.
activeFindings.gate: Before implementing or accepting the new clinic behavior test
